helper.title: Add flour
descriptions: Add flour gradually, mixing with a wooden spoon until you get a homogeneous mixture

restRT.title: Rest { rtRestTime } hour(s) at room temperature

helper.title: Rest at room temperature
descriptions: Let rest { rtRestTime } hour(s) at room temperature in an airtight container or covered with plastic wrap
The rest will allow the yeast to activate, create a beautiful gluten network and thus give all its texture to the dough
The dough will tighten and become smoother

helper.title: Rest in refrigerator
descriptions: Let rest { coldRestTime } hour(s) in refrigerator in an airtight container or covered with plastic wrap
The rest will allow the yeast to activate, create a beautiful gluten network and thus give all its texture to the dough
The dough will tighten and become smoother

helper.title: How to use poolish
descriptions: Take out poolish 1 hour before use, so it has time to return to room temperature

addWaterSalt.title: {hasSalt, select, true {In poolish, add water and salt} other {In poolish, add water}}

helper.title: Dough preparation
descriptions: Weigh the quantities to add to poolish
{hasSalt, select, true {In the poolish bowl, add water and salt. Mix with wooden spoon until water is absorbed} other {In the poolish bowl, add water. Mix with wooden spoon until water is absorbed}}

helper.title: How to add flour
descriptions: Add flour little by little and mix with wooden spoon

helper.title: Dough transfer
descriptions: When it's no longer possible to mix with the spoon, we start to have a dough appearance and can transfer it to the work surface
Use a pastry scraper to help with the transfer

helper.title: Kneading
descriptions: Work the dough by kneading it for about 10 min, flour must be completely integrated
Use the palm of your hands to knead
You can also use a stand mixer with its dough hook, but it's less fun 😉

foldAndShape.title: Make a few folds and form a ball

helper.title: Folds
descriptions: To make a fold, take the dough and fold it on itself
You can make as many folds as you want, but the dough must remain soft and supple
The fold allows air to be introduced into the dough and will allow an airy texture when baking
Once finished, you can form a beautiful ball

helper.title: Rest
descriptions: Simply turn over the bowl used for preparation on the dough
The dough will tighten and become smoother

helper.title: Form a ball
descriptions: Don't work the dough too much
Stretch the dough and by making it turn a few times between your hands, reform a ball

helper.title: Forming dough balls
descriptions: Take the dough and with the help of a dough cutter or spatula
Form dough balls (well stretched) of about { pizzaWeight } g
Put a thin layer of fine semolina in a dish (this will prevent them from sticking to the dish)
Place dough balls in a dish leaving space between them (they will still grow)
Close the dish or put plastic wrap

helper.title: Dough ball rest
descriptions: The resting time of dough ball varies depending on temperature
It takes about { rtRestTime } hour(s), so remember to take it into account 😉
